prose.title: Sex Manther Tagged McCaffrey, Threw Him Back, and Bought Lamar Jackson
prose.dek: Josh Martel released {{f.team.0007.cuts_s2_salary}} of salary before the auction lock, spent {{f.team.0007.top_buy_price}} on Lamar Jackson, and front-loaded Rashee Rice with what was left. The preseason simulation ranks Sex Manther {{f.team.0007.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was expensive. Martel carried {{f.team.0007.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0007.cap_opening}} in salary, with {{f.team.0007.studs_opening}} top-twelve starters: Caleb Williams, a High-end QB1, Christian McCaffrey and De'Von Achane at running back, and Harold Fannin and George Kittle at tight end. Rashee Rice was solid at receiver. The {{f.team.0007.holes_opening}} holes were Rome Odunze at the second receiver spot, Jacory Croskey-Merritt in a flex, and Jonathon Brooks, a running back, in the superflex.

Martel already had Christian McCaffrey on a {{f.team.0007.contract_13130_salary}} tag by April. The spring trades were all about picks, and the trade bot was not grading deals yet; graded now on what was known on each trade's date, they come out {{f.team.0007.trade1_grade}} and {{f.team.0007.trade2_grade}}. In March Martel sent 1.10 to Blake Bombers for their 2027 first, and in May he sent 3.04 and 3.06 to The Long Haulers for five later picks; 3.06 went on through Gride to Real Deal Creel, who used it on Sonny Styles. He made no cuts or extensions, and no rookie deals ran out on him.

t.0007.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: McCaffrey was the chip. A tag in this league is something to trade, to keep, or to hand back, and in July Martel handed it back, releasing McCaffrey with no penalty and keeping all {{f.team.0007.cut_13130_salary}} of the tag money to spend on other players.

In June he extended Rice for {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_years}} years at a TCV of {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_tcv}}, back-loaded: {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_next_salary}} next. The room came in July: Kittle and his {{f.team.0007.trade3_salary_out}} salary went to Blake Bombers with {{f.team.0007.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money for a 2027 second, a {{f.team.0007.trade3_grade}} from the trade bot on its second look, Efton Chism went to Cleon Ca$h for a 2027 fifth, a {{f.team.0007.trade4_grade}}, and the day before the lock Martel cut Tyreek Hill, {{f.team.0007.cut_12801_salary}} of salary with a {{f.team.0007.cut_12801_penalty}} penalty. The draft, {{f.team.0007.rookie_picks_count}} picks from 3.11 down, was mostly defenders, and Sean Tucker came from the Expired Rookie Auction for {{f.team.0007.era_16166_price}}.

The roster held at {{f.team.0007.active_roster_preauction}} active players while the salary fell from {{f.team.0007.cap_opening}} to {{f.team.0007.cap_preauction}}. McCaffrey, Hill and Kittle were most of the difference, and the day before the auction Martel restructured Achane and Rice down to {{f.team.0007.contract_16167_salary}} and {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_salary_2}} this year, which did most of the rest; the room was the point.

t.0007.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Sex Manther spent {{f.team.0007.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction. Lamar Jackson cost {{f.team.0007.faa_13593_price}} after twelve bids, Jaylen Waddle {{f.team.0007.faa_15284_price}}, Jameson Williams {{f.team.0007.faa_15756_price}} and Kenny Gainwell {{f.team.0007.faa_15255_price}}, part of {{f.team.0007.faa_lots_won}} wins that also included a punter, Ryan Eckley, for {{f.team.0007.faa_17664_price}}, whom Martel claimed in the chat as his punter while the bidding was still open.

What it bought: Jackson, the one Very good buy, and Waddle and Jameson Williams, two Good ones; the rest is bench depth. The league table ranks Sex Manther {{f.team.0007.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for how much the auction improved the offense, and with Caleb Williams in the superflex his quarterbacks rank {{f.team.0007.qb_rank|ord}} in the league.

The contracts that followed were long. Jackson signed for {{f.team.0007.contract_13593_years}} years at a TCV of {{f.team.0007.contract_13593_tcv}}, back-loaded: {{f.team.0007.contract_13593_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0007.contract_13593_next_salary}} in 2027. Waddle signed for {{f.team.0007.contract_15284_years}} years at {{f.team.0007.contract_15284_salary}} a year and Williams for {{f.team.0007.contract_15756_years}} at {{f.team.0007.contract_15756_salary}}. The room left over after the auction did not go to waste: in September Martel restructured Rice the other way, front-loading him to {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_salary_3}} this year and {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_next_salary_3}} in 2027. He claimed {{f.team.0007.pickups_s3}} players off waivers before week one, released Tucker and seven others at no cost, two taxi-squad players and five he had signed this offseason, and traded Gunnar Helm to The Long Haulers for a 2027 fifth, a {{f.team.0007.trade5_grade}} from the bot.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0007.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Jackson, Caleb Williams, Achane and Fannin, with Rice, Waddle and Jameson Williams solid at receiver, and {{f.team.0007.holes_today}} holes: Croskey-Merritt at the second running back spot and Odunze in a flex. Graded on MFL's projections the defense is a strength, Tuli Tuipulotu a High-end DL1, Julian Love a High-end DB1, and the rookie Dillon Thieneman already a starter. The kicker, Eddy Pineiro, is replacement-level.

Three starters are questionable for the opener, Odunze with a calf, Croskey-Merritt with a groin and Tuipulotu with a hip; none is listed out, so the forecast plays them all, and MarShawn Lloyd is next up at running back, with Jonathon Brooks behind him questionable too. Tank Dell is on injured reserve into October, and Jayden Higgins, on the taxi squad, is out for the season.

captions.t.0007.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close; a buy that never makes the lineup adds nothing. What it bought grades each quarterback, back, receiver and tight end at his position: Elite is this year's separated top, which is one man at some positions and nobody at others, Very good the rest of the top twelve, Good the next twelve at quarterback, back and receiver (every team starts two, counting the superflex), Starter depth anyone else who starts somewhere in the league, and Bench depth the rest.

paragraphs: Martel arrived in {{f.team.0007.hist_first_season}}, and in {{f.team.0007.hist_seasons}} seasons he has built one of the league's best records: back-to-back titles in 2019 and 2020, runner-up in 2018 and 2025, {{f.team.0007.hist_div_titles}} division titles and {{f.team.0007.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips, and a {{f.team.0007.hist_allplay_pct}} career all-play record.

He drafted this division himself, and for the rivalry. Seated {{f.league.div_draft_captain_0007|ord}} among the captains, Martel had said in May that some captains would pick for fun rather than for the weakest team left, and then took Real Deal Creel {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0008|ord}} overall and doubled back for L.A. Looks {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0001|ord}}. Maddie Mondays is now the closest division in the simulation: Real Deal Creel {{f.league.p_division_0008}}, Sex Manther {{f.team.0007.sim_p_division}} and L.A. Looks {{f.league.p_division_0001}}, with {{f.team.0007.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds for Martel.

The byes fall his way. The division weeks are {{f.team.0007.div_weeks}}, and across all five he loses {{f.team.0007.div_week_own_byes}} starters to byes, L.A. Looks {{f.team.0007.div_week_byes_0001}} and Real Deal Creel {{f.team.0007.div_week_byes_0008}}. Week eight costs him only Pineiro, week eleven Fannin, Carson Schwesinger and Julian Love, and week fourteen, the last of the regular season, nobody at all, while L.A. Looks loses three Cowboys and Real Deal Creel loses Dak Prescott.

The next three years, Martel style. 2027: Lamar. Achane. Blake's first-round pick. The broom comes out 🧹 and the division is his. 2028: Real Deal Creel takes the division from him, and Martel reminds Real Deal Creel which of them has the rings. 2029: L.A. Looks takes Maddie Mondays, and Sex Manther watches the playoffs from home.

Week one is a division week. With {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Julian Love had an interception, Pineiro hit a long field goal, and Sex Manther has {{f.team.0007.wk_points_final}} points in the bank. Martel has already told Real Deal Creel, in reply to one of its week-one waiver claims, that none of it is going to be enough.
